question: Give the vector equation of a line passing through the point $(1,2,-1)$ and parallel to the vector $2\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j} + 3\mathbf{k}$.
explanation:
The position vector of the point $(1,2,-1)$ is $\vec{a}=\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j}-\mathbf{k}$.

The direction vector is $\vec{b}=2\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}+3\mathbf{k}$.

The vector equation of a line is given by $\vec{r}=\vec{a}+\lambda \vec{b}$.

Substituting the values gives $\vec{r}=(\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j}-\mathbf{k})+\lambda(2\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}+3\mathbf{k})$.
